title: M7.P1: Cloud layout changes as numbered, repeatable steps — a layout marker in the cloud and a migration ladder, not one-offs
body:
## M7.P1 source implementation — 2026-10-03

The strict marker reader now validates complete layout1/layout2 bytes; unsupported values cannot authorize default-layout merges, pointer transitions or seeding. The shared writer checks publication and reads it back. Explicit migration_step_1 keeps original sources and configured choices in an atomic, synchronized local JSON record before any tier mutation; numbered journal events identify progress. Copy, deletion or marker failure retains that record. Boot/scan expose an interrupted move as TRY AGAIN / NOT NOW; token refresh does not invalidate the configured-remote fingerprint. The record is not a distributed cloud lock.

Evidence: docs/qa-logs/2026-10-03-m7-p1/. The12 malformed/future/trailing marker controls fail on fcd0f20c9a and pass after. Final9 copy/delete/marker retry controls fail before and pass after, including byte preservation, visible retry, idempotence and a follower without local mover state. All93 focused cases and1,367 broad host checks pass. ES39f8883545537d5274708ea85c4683612078a957 includes the retry UI (68e8c7da5) and settings race fix; image compiler and French catalog checks pass.

Already written: older runs may have advanced some pointers without a complete marker; no data is inferred or overwritten from marker presence alone. The new record covers interruptions originating in this implementation. Actual predecessor partial states, actor coverage and two-guest/provider/upgrade/frame proof remain open and must be qualified on the candidate. No acceptance criterion requiring a VM is ticked by these host results.

## Source review — 2026-10-02 (#385)

The general version contract is still unimplemented. `fleet_made()` accepts any `layout=` prefix, `write_marker()` returns success on failed publication, and tiers may publish pointers before a later refusal. `cloud_setup` also writes markers. T23's host collision case does not prove interrupted retry or fleet recovery. The 0.0.1 gate includes explicit version parsing, numbered transitions/journal, interruption/retry and marker-publication failure. See docs/rasteratops/cloud-layout.md and release-readiness.md.

Compatibility boundary: a new build cannot make the already shipped RC2 binary understand a new protocol. The proof must name the predecessor binaries and show their actual behaviour. Future-version handling below is exercised with the version-aware implementation offered a newer synthetic marker, while the RC2→candidate upgrade and mixed-installation proof remain separate required cases. Do not infer a fleet-wide-upgrade prerequisite from D-CLOUD-169.

## The maintainer's words (2026-10-01, on moving the Nova's cloud)

> Agreed that we need to move Nova's cloud. We should also always be thinking about the upgrade path, and so this might be something where we want to think about not just doing it as a one-off, but how this would happen for changes on an ongoing basis.

## The shape proposed

A cloud layout has a version. The cloud root carries a small marker (`/Rasteratops/.layout`, one line: `layout=2`), written by the device that creates or moves the folders; each device compares the marker with the layout its build expects and runs the numbered steps between them, one step at a time, each step a copy-verify-delete with its own one-time dialog (D-CLOUD-160's MOVE / KEEP / NOT NOW) and its own journal line. Step 1 is `/GAMES` and `/ROCKNIX` to `/Rasteratops` (#353); a later change is step 2, written once, and every device in the fleet takes it when it next checks. A device on a newer layout than the marker never writes the old shape; a device on an older build than the marker reads what it can and says so (`upgrade-and-install.md`: old code reads new data). The marker is data, not a lock: two devices racing to move is prevented by the copy-then-verify order, not by the marker.

## Can this be done on the VM?

**Yes**: `tools/vm-pair` with two guests on one QA cloud, one on the old layout, and `cloud_migrate_layout` driven through the interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cloud_migrate_layout` runs numbered steps from the marker's version to the build's, each with the move dialog, each copy-verify-delete, each a journal line naming the step; a `tools/cloud-round-trip` case seeds layout 1 and ends at layout 2 with the marker written and nothing lost (hash list before and after).
- [ ] A second guest on the same cloud takes the new marker at its next check with no dialog (its journal line), and the version-aware candidate offered a newer or malformed marker refuses unsupported writes/marker overwrite, showing a supported outcome (frame plus byte/pointer assertions). The separate RC2→candidate and mixed-installation receipts name the actual old binary and prove preservation; they do not claim RC2 implements this future protocol.
- [ ] Fault injection after each completed tier and at marker publication followed by retry preserves both sides, completes without duplicate/lost state, and lets a second guest follow; logs identify the numbered step and hashes.
- [ ] The step for `/GAMES` and `/ROCKNIX` is step 1 and is the one #353 ships; the design note lives in `docs/rasteratops/cloud-layout.md`.
